Create a template yaml file for supplying attribute metadata for a data object that cannot be read into R

write_other_attributes.Rd

write_other_attributes creates a template as a yaml file for supplying attribute metadata for an otherEntity (e.g., a zip file of LiDAR point clouds in LAZ format) that cannot be read into the R environment. Unlike write_attributes, which derives a template from a data object in R, the names and classes of the attributes are provided by the user.

Usage

write_other_attributes(
  target_file,
  attributes,
  column_classes = "character",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  metadata_path = NULL
)

Arguments

target_file

(character) The quoted name of the data file (e.g., "lidar_tiles.zip"). The file is used only to name the template; it does not need to be readable.

attributes

(character) The names of the attributes (variables) in the data object.

column_classes

(character) The class of each attribute: numeric, character, factor, or Date. A single value applies to all attributes. Defaults to character.

overwrite

(logical) Logical indicating if an existing attributes file in the target directory should be overwritten.

metadata_path

(character) Directory to which the template is written. Defaults to metadata_path in config.yaml, else the working directory.

Value

The path to the template is returned invisibly, and a template for providing attribute metadata is written to metadata_path.

Details

The template is named for the target file without its extension (e.g., lidar_tiles.zip yields lidar_tiles_attrs.yaml) and written to metadata_path. create_otherEntity reads the annotated template and adds the metadata to the attributeList of the resulting otherEntity. The EML schema permits an attributeList for any otherEntity regardless of file format.

When to use

Attributes describe variables or fields that exist within the data object, such as the point record fields (e.g., X, Y, Z, Classification) of LiDAR point clouds in a zip file, the attribute table of a zipped shapefile, the value classes of a raster, or the columns of spreadsheets in a zip file. Each attribute must correspond to a variable in the object.

Required fields by column class

Every attribute requires an attributeDefinition. Additional fields depend on columnClasses:

numeric

unit (an EML standard unit, see EML::get_unitList(), or a custom unit, which is documented in custom_units.yaml when the EML is built) and numberType (one of natural, whole, integer, real). minimum and maximum are optional and must be entered manually.

character

no additional fields; leave definition blank as it is populated from attributeDefinition.

factor

the codes and their definitions are provided in a factors template (see write_other_factors).

Date

formatString describing the format of the date or time (e.g., YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY, hh:mm:ss).

The propertyURI, propertyLabel, valueURI, and valueLabel fields are optional semantic annotations. create_otherEntity stops and lists any missing required fields.

What is not allowed

Attributes are not a place for metadata about the file itself (e.g., author, number of files in an archive, version, software used to create it); provide those details in the description or additional_information arguments of create_otherEntity, the methods, or dataset-level metadata. Do not invent attributes that do not exist in the object.

Limitations

Because the data are not read, minimum and maximum cannot be calculated, and missing value codes are not detected or supported in these templates.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

 # point record fields of the LiDAR point clouds (LAZ) in a zip file

 capeml::write_other_attributes(
   target_file    = "lidar_tiles.zip",
   attributes     = c("X", "Y", "Z", "Classification", "GpsTime"),
   column_classes = c("numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "factor", "numeric")
 )

} # }
